newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nuclear waste cargo to stay out of S.African waters.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste cargo to stay out of S.African waters.

text.p: South Africa's environment ministry on Thursday said a planned nuclear waste shipment from Europe to Japan would not enter the country's waters.
The environmental group Greenpeace said on Wednesday that a shipment of plutonium waste was expected to pass through the Tasman Sea, between Australia and New Zealand, in February.

Greenpeace, citing what it said was a leaked French diplomatic document, said the cargo would contain 40 canisters of plutonium waste encased in glass blocks and carried on the British-registered Pacific Teal to Japan.
South Africa's Department of Environmental Affairs and Tourism said in statement that Environmental Affairs Minister Pallo Jordan expected confirmation of the ship's route next week.
"Minister Jordan has, however, received assurances that the ship will not pass through South African territorial waters," the statement said.
Jordan was briefed on the nuclear waste cargo by officials from French industrial group COGEMA and Japanese electrical power companies, his spokeswoman Cassandra Gabriel told Reuters.
The statement said that the South Africans had been briefed on security measures put in place to safeguard the shipment and the environment.
The nuclear waste was produced in the reprocessing, in France, of spent Japanese nuclear fuel to extract plutonium.

Pacific Teal is scheduled to leave France on January 16 and sail via South Africa, Australia and the South Pacific, a route used for a previous shipment in 1992. Another shipment sailed around the southern tip of South America in 1995.
